title: Accounts Payable Coordinator
description:
As an Accounts Payable Coordinator in a research-led organisation, based in Oxfordshire, you'll manage supplier invoices, payments, and queries to ensure smooth day-to-day operations. Your role will help keep financial processes accurate and efficient, supporting the wider accounting and finance team.

Client Details

A company in the innovative technology sector located in Oxfordshire.

Description
- Process supplier invoices and ensure timely payments.
- Handle supplier queries and resolve discrepancies efficiently.
- Maintain accurate records of accounts payable transactions.
- Reconcile supplier statements and resolve outstanding issues.
- Support month-end close processes by providing necessary documentation.
- Assist with audits by preparing and organising relevant financial data.
- Ensure compliance with company policies and financial regulations.
- Collaborate with other departments for smooth financial operations.

Profile

A successful Accounts Payable Coordinator should have:
- Experience working with accounting and finance systems.
- Strong attention to detail and organisational skills.
- Ability to handle supplier queries and resolve issues effectively.
- Familiarity with accounts payable processes and reconciliations.
- Knowledge of financial regulations and compliance requirements.
- Good communication and teamwork skills.

Job Offer
- Salary ranging from £28,000 to £35,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Competitive benefits package.
- Flexible working options.
- Supportive team culture.
- Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

People are at the heart of Michael Page. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment. As an inclusive recruiter we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and experiences. If you require any adjustments or accommodations during the recruitment process, we'll work with you to ensure you can perform at your best.

title: Accounts Receivable Assistant - Cash Allocation
description:
Cash Allocation Specialist Didcot (Hybrid) Permanent Up to £30,000

The Opportunity

IN2 Consult is partnering with a market leading business based near Didcot, to recruit a Cash Allocation Specialist into its Accounts Receivable team. This is a busy, high-volume role at the centre of the order-to-cash process. You will make sure customer receipts are matched, posted and reconciled accurately and on time, so the sales ledger always shows a true picture of what the business is owed.

Key Responsibilities
- Allocate daily customer receipts from BACS, CHAPS, card and cheque payments against open invoices on the sales ledger
- Match remittance advices to payments, investigating and resolving unallocated or unidentified cash
- Reconcile customer accounts and clear historic unallocated balances and suspense items
- Post receipts accurately within agreed daily deadlines
- Work with Credit Control to resolve queries, short payments, overpayments and deductions
- Raise and process customer refunds and credit notes in line with approval controls
- Support the daily bank reconciliation and month-end close, including aged debt reporting
- Contact customers and internal teams to get missing remittance information
- Identify process improvements that cut unallocated cash and speed up allocation

About You
- Previous experience in cash allocation, cash posting, sales ledger or accounts receivable
- Comfortable working through high transaction volumes quickly without losing accuracy
- Good working knowledge of Excel (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables, filters)
- Experience with various ERP systems
- Strong attention to detail with a methodical, problem-solving approach
- Confident communicator, by phone and email, with customers and colleagues
- Able to prioritise a daily workload against firm deadlines

Desirable: AAT studier or interest in studying, shared service centre experience, multi-currency or multi-entity allocation.

title: Finance Administrator
description:
- Finance Administrator - Sales Ledger
- Deddington, Oxfordshire Hybrid
- £27,000 + up to 10% Annual Bonus
- Permanent Full-Time 37.5 hours per week

An excellent opportunity has arisen for a Finance Administrator to join a successful, employee-owned business based on the outskirts of Banbury, Oxfordshire (5 miles from Banbury/accessible by public transport).

This is a varied position with a strong focus on sales ledger and would suit someone in the early stages of their finance career who has gained around 1-2 years' experience and is now looking for their next step.

You'll be joining a friendly and supportive finance team within an established business that genuinely values its people. There will be plenty of opportunity to build on your existing finance experience, take on more responsibility and develop your career over time.

The Role

Working as part of the finance team, your responsibilities will include:
- Raising sales invoices
- Maintaining and reconciling the Sales Ledger
- Receipting and reconciling client purchase orders
- Monitoring un-invoiced balances, debtors and landed margin
- Proactive credit control and chasing overdue payments
- Preparing and issuing client statements
- Managing client rebates
- Producing Sales Ledger reports for management
- Managing the finance inbox and responding to queries
- Providing Purchase Ledger cover when required
- Credit card administration and reconciliations
- Supporting PO approvals and wider finance administration
- Looking for opportunities to improve processes and make better use of technology and AI

About You

We're looking for someone with:
- Around 1-2 years' experience within finance/accounts, potentially gained after university, college or leaving school
- Some previous exposure to sales ledger, accounts receivable, invoicing or credit control
- Good attention to detail and organisational skills
- A proactive, positive and reliable approach
- A professional approach, with good communication skills and confidence dealing with customers
- Comfortable using Excel and finance systems
- An interest in using technology to improve processes and ways of working
- Sage experience would be advantageous, but isn't essential

This would suit someone who has gained a good foundation in finance and is keen to learn, develop and take the next step in their career.

What's on Offer?
- £27,000 salary
- Annual bonus of up to 10%
- Hybrid working
- 20 days' holiday + bank holidays, rising annually to 25 days
- Life cover and wellness benefits
- Employee Assistance Programme for you and your family
- Weekly and quarterly recognition awards
- Training budget and ongoing development support
- Employee-owned business
- Supportive, professional and friendly working environment
- Opportunity to broaden your finance experience and develop over time

If you've gained your first year or two of experience within finance and are looking for an opportunity to develop within a supportive business, please apply or get in touch with The Employment Network for more information.

title: Finance Assistant - Sales Ledger
description:
Finance Assistant - Sales Ledger
Permanent, Full-Time (37.5 hours per week)
Deddington, Oxfordshire

About the Employer
An innovative and collaborative organisation operating within the marketing and communications sector, supporting well-known brands through creative thinking, commercial expertise and technology. With a strong focus on people, innovation and continuous improvement, the business combines specialist knowledge with smart digital tools to deliver effective solutions in a fast-changing environment.

About the Role
This is an exciting opportunity for a motivated Finance Assistant to develop their finance career within a supportive and forward-thinking team. You'll help keep day-to-day financial processes running smoothly, with a particular focus on sales ledger administration, invoicing, reconciliations and credit control. You'll also provide purchase ledger and wider operational support while helping identify smarter ways of working. If you're organised, detail-focused and curious about technology and AI, this is an excellent opportunity to build your finance experience and make a real contribution.

Duties & Responsibilities
- Raise sales invoices and ensure the Sales Ledger is accurate, up to date and fully reconciled.
- Receipt and reconcile client purchase orders, while monitoring un-invoiced balances, debtors and landed margin.
- Carry out proactive credit control, including following up overdue payments and preparing and issuing client statements.
- Manage client rebates and support accurate Sales Ledger records and reporting for management.
- Manage the finance inbox, responding to queries promptly and providing a helpful and professional service.
- Provide Purchase Ledger cover when required, including credit card administration and reconciliations.
- Support purchase order approvals and wider finance administration, working collaboratively with colleagues across the business.
- Identify opportunities to improve finance processes, increase efficiency and make better use of technology, automation and AI.

Education & Skills Required
- Desirable if you are studying towards an AAT qualification, have previous experience in an Accounts Administrator, Finance Assistant or similar role, or be a recent graduate with a relevant degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related subject.
- Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail, accuracy and time management.
- Confident communicator who works well as part of a collaborative team.
- Proactive, reliable and positive, with a willingness to take ownership and find solutions.
- Good computer skills and an interest in digital technology, automation and AI.
- Experience using SAGE or a similar finance system would be advantageous.

Additional Information
- £27,000 salary
- Annual bonus of up to 10%
- Full-time, permanent position, Monday to Friday
- Hybrid working, with Fridays working from home
- 20 days' holiday plus bank holidays, increasing annually to 25 days
- Life cover and wellness benefits
- Training budget and ongoing professional development support
- Supportive, professional and friendly working environment
- Opportunity to broaden your finance experience and develop your career over time

If you're looking to develop your finance career and have the organisation, attention to detail and positive attitude to succeed, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today and join a collaborative team where your ideas and contribution can make a real difference.

title: HR and Payroll Officer
company: Not For Profit People - Agency - Permanent
description:
HR and Payroll Officer

Are you an organised and people-focused HR professional with payroll experience who enjoys delivering excellent service and building strong working relationships?

We are seeking an enthusiastic HR and Payroll Officer to join the Human Resources team in this full-time, permanent role.

This role offers the opportunity to work across the full employee lifecycle while building expertise in both HR and payroll. It is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing attention to detail with relationship-building and who takes pride in delivering a high-quality service.

Position: HR & Payroll Officer

Location: Kidlington, Oxford/hybrid

Hours: Full-time, 37 hours per week

Salary: £37,751.95 - £40,655.94 per annum

Contract: Permanent

Closing Date: Midnight on Tuesday 18 November 2026. Interviews will take place at Church House, Oxford: Friday 27 November 2026

The Role

You will join the Human Resources team, playing a key role in supporting employees, clergy, managers and senior leaders across the Diocese. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to meaningful work, ensuring people are supported through efficient payroll, recruitment, learning and development, and employee lifecycle processes.

This is a varied and rewarding role within a professional and collaborative HR team that supports both the Diocesan Board of Finance and Diocesan Board of Education. You will provide reliable, confidential and people-centred HR and payroll support that helps employees, clergy and leaders do their best work.

You will also play a key role in delivering recruitment and onboarding activities, be the first point of contact for payroll-related matters and will help maintain robust controls and ensure compliance with statutory and organisational requirements.

About You

We are looking for an experienced HR and payroll professional who is highly organised, accurate and customer-focused, with a passion for providing excellent support and advice. You will be comfortable managing multiple priorities, handling sensitive information with discretion and working collaboratively with a wide range of stakeholders.

You will bring experience of HR administration and payroll processing within a busy organisational environment, together with strong communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving.

You will also have:
- Sound knowledge of generalist HR practices and payroll administration.
- Up-to-date knowledge of UK employment legislation and HMRC requirements relating to payroll, tax and statutory payments.
- Experience supporting recruitment, onboarding, learning and development, employee relations and performance management activities.
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications, and experience using HR management systems and payroll systems.
- High levels of accuracy and attention to detail, particularly when working with payroll and employee data and maintaining accurate employee records.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.

A CIPD and/or CIPP qualification or membership would be advantageous, although applications are welcomed from candidates with transferable skills and experience.

You do not need to be a practising Christian to work here. Around half of staff are not practising Christians, but all are comfortable working within the Christian ethos and values that underpin the organisation's work.

The successful candidate must have the right to live and work in the United Kingdom. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for interviews. We are particularly keen to receive applications from UK Minority Ethnic / Global Majority heritage and disabled candidates, who are currently underrepresented.

You may have experience in other areas such as HR, Human Resources, Personnel, People, HR Officer, Human Resources Officer, Personnel Officer, People Officer, Payroll, Payroll Officer, Payroll Assistant, HR Assistant, Finance Officer, Finance Assistant, HR and Finance, HR and Payroll.

Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People.

title: Part-Time Accounts Assistant
description:
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced accounts and administration professional to provide support across a variety of business, charity and property matters.

Working for a client based near Henley-on-Thames, you will assist with accounts and general administration tasks, with support from an external accountant. This varied role would suit someone who is organised, enjoys working independently and is confident keeping track of different responsibilities and deadlines.

£18.50 per hour.

10 hours per week over two days, with flexibility on the days and times worked.

Due to the location, you will need to drive.

Responsibilities:
- Maintain the diary, provide meeting reminders and ensure information is prepared in advance
- Monitor emails and assist with typing, scanning and general correspondence
- Keep office supplies and stationery up to date
- Maintain financial records and prepare supporting information for monthly and annual accounts, working with the external accountant
- Collate financial information for VAT returns, with support from the external accountant
- Monitor bank accounts and maintain cashflow records
- Set up invoices for payment and prepare monthly payroll information for a small number of employees, with payroll processed by the accountants
- Monitor rental payments and issue rent demands
- Maintain tenant records, deposit information and tenancy schedules
- Keep track of lease renewals and provide reminders
- Produce an annual service charge
- Liaise with tenants, accountants and solicitors as required
- Maintain tenant email groups and contact details
- Keep track of projects and deadlines, including buildings insurance and gas certificates
- Make occasional trips to the bank and post office
- Assist with other day-to-day tasks as needed

Experience and skills required:
- Previous experience in a varied accounts and administration role
- Experience maintaining financial records and preparing information
- Confidence monitoring bank accounts, payments and cashflow
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage a variety of tasks and deadlines
- Accuracy and attention to detail
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- Confidence liaising with tenants and professional contacts
- A proactive approach and the ability to work independently
- Property administration experience would be useful
- The ability to drive due to the location

title: Temp to Perm Payroll Officer
